newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico governor says Guerrero state under control.
newsitem.headline: Mexico governor says Guerrero state under control.

text.p: Military authorities have restored order in the southwestern Mexican state of Guerrero, shaken by recent clashes between guerrillas and the military, the state governor said on Thursday.
"Everything is under control and up to now there have been no more clashes," governor Angel Aguirre Rivero said at a news conference.
Army troops and rebels of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) have fought several times in the past few days in the poor state -- their first clashes this year.
The army said on Thursday at least nine soldiers and rebels were killed in the fighting. The Marxist rebels claim at least 60 people have been killed or wounded.
Aguirre said, however, that there were five dead soldiers and 13 wounded, while the rebels lost four fighters.
Earlier in the day the Mexican army denied it had captured a top commander of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) guerrilla group.
A military source had said late on Wednesday that the army captured an EPR leader known as Commander Hermenegildo during a gunbattle on Tuesday in the southwestern state of Guerrero.
But the 9th Military Region, which has jurisdiction over the state, said in a statement the report published by Mexican media "lacked foundation and it is not known who started it."
Hermenegildo was the name used by the author of several communiques sent by the Marxist rebel group involved in at least two gunbattles with authorities since Saturday.
